title: The Markov family's shared parameter definitions
description: What the Markov family's two versions, artificial and zero-infima, have in common, as model.md names it. Each version's parameters.schema.json takes these definitions and adds its family key and constraint. Draft.

period.description: The length of a period, as a label. Every rate and probability in the file is per period.

crra.description: rho, the coefficient of relative risk aversion, greater than 1 as in BST.

splurge.description: The splurge, the share of income consumed before the choice; 0 for none (model.md, 'The splurge, as an observation map').

survival.description: The survival probability (BST's script L); 1 switches mortality off.

return.description: R, the gross return on assets, earned by survivors.

employed_shock.description: The law of theta, the employed draw, scaled by income_employed.

regimes.description: The aggregate regimes. The normal regime has no key, since it is absorbing.

exit_hazard.description: p_exit, the probability that a recession ends in a period.

benefit_quarters.description: The periods of benefits; 2 for the stage file's chain.

job_finding.description: find, the probability of finding a job in a period, by regime; positive, so that unemployment is not absorbing.

income_employed.description: e, the scale of employed income e theta.

income_with_benefits.description: xi_u, income with benefits, as a ratio to permanent income.

income_without_benefits.description: xi_x, income after benefits expire, as a ratio to permanent income.

unemployed_permanent_income.description: P_u, permanent income in a period of unemployment: continues (G psi applies), grows (G applies and psi = 1) or frozen (unchanged). Never omitted.

groups.description: The groups, each with its own growth, job loss, newborn law and discount-factor types; shares summing to one.

growth.description: The group's growth factor of permanent income (BST's script G).

job_loss.description: sep, the probability of losing a job in a period, by regime.

newborn_income.description: The newborn's permanent income, a lognormal in the levels of the period's units, by its median and the standard deviation of its log: HARK's exp(pLogInitMean) and pLogInitStd.

types.description: The discount-factor types, in increasing order of beta, with shares summing to one within the group.

artificial_constraint.description: The artificial borrowing constraint a_Art, the lowest permitted end-of-period assets as a ratio to permanent income, in the household's units: a number no greater than 0, strictly above the lowest natural limit a_Nat(j), which the checker enforces.
